candidate.source: this change rebased onto that main; the measured tree matches the pull request apart from documentation

main.source: origin/main 07c15d5e93, which includes the generation storage of #9790

binaries.profile: release, thin LTO, 16 codegen units, Rust 1.95.0

cold_selected_default.cap: available parallelism minus the publisher and trigram installer threads, at least one
cold_selected_default.reason: Six workers were faster than four in all twelve paired rounds of two matrices (median 0.87 and 0.91 of four-worker readiness) for 9-12% more CPU and about 1.5% more peak memory. The publisher bounds the build beyond that, so more workers were not measured.

corpus.source: private copy of the frozen #9712 corpus, so concurrent restart benchmarks cannot rewrite its seed

protocol.cold_matrix: six rounds; each round runs main and the candidate at 1, 2, 4, and 6 fact workers in an order rotated per round
protocol.pmu: not collected; phases are wall-clock sums per phase name, so worker phases add across threads
protocol.readiness: build plus snapshot save, before the registered Cypher, word, trigram, and literal queries, all of which must pass
protocol.refresh_pairs: four alternating pairs each of the head and batch64 scenarios against main, at the four fact workers that were the default when they ran
protocol.regime: shared host: CI kept 1 to 7 cores busy through nearly every trial, so 2 of 30 cold trials were accepted. All complete rounds are reported; paired rotation is what makes them comparable, and absolute times run about 29% above the quiet #9712 baseline.

batch64.parity: graph, postings, and corpus digests plus file, node, edge, and resolved-call counts equal in every pair

head.parity: graph, postings, and corpus digests plus file, node, edge, and resolved-call counts equal in every pair
